recipes.source_title: Crispy Potatoes with Lemon and Feta Recipe
recipes.summary: Crispy Potatoes with Lemon and Feta is a sattvic vegetarian dish of new potatoes, organic extra virgin olive oil, organic dried oregano. No onion or garlic — hing bloomed in hot oil gives the savoury depth. Cook fresh and serve as prasad-style kitchen food.
ingredients: 3 tbsp organic extra virgin olive oil
100 g crumbled paneer or plant feta, crumbled
Small handful fresh mint, finely chopped

ingredient_groups.name: For the potatoes :
items: 3 tbsp organic extra virgin olive oil

ingredient_groups.name: To serve :
items: 100 g crumbled paneer or plant feta, crumbled
Small handful fresh mint, finely chopped

method: Start by placing the new potatoes in a pan of cold, salted water.
Bring to the boil, then simmer until just tender.
Drain well, then leave them to steam dry and cool slightly so they’re easier to handle.
While the potatoes are cooling, add the a pinch of hing to a small bowl with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Toss together and leave to soften and lightly pickle.
Once cooled, place the potatoes on a large roasting tray and gently crush each one with the back of a spoon or a glass so they flatten and split slightly.
This helps create lots of crispy edges.
Drizzle over the olive oil, scatter with oregano, salt and pepper, then add the lemon slices to the tray.
Toss everything gently so the potatoes are coated without breaking them up too much.
Roast in a hot oven until the potatoes are deeply golden and crisp on the edges, turning once during cooking.
The lemon slices will soften and caramelise, becoming sweet and slightly jammy.
Transfer the hot potatoes to a serving dish, then scatter with crumbled feta so it softens slightly.
Finish with the fresh mint and the lightly pickled celery over the top.
Serve straight away while warm, with extra roasted lemon on the side for squeezing over.

recipes.summary: Easy Sourdough is a sattvic vegetarian dish of organic strong white bread flour, lukewarm water, active sourdough starter. No onion or garlic — hing bloomed in hot oil gives the savoury depth. Cook fresh and serve as prasad-style kitchen food.
ingredients: 500 g organic strong white bread flour

items: 500 g organic strong white bread flour

method: Place the flour in a large bowl and mix in the sourdough starter.
Slowly pour in the water while mixing with your hands or a spoon until a sticky dough forms.
Cover and leave for 30 minutes to rest.
Sprinkle over the salt and gently knead it into the dough.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic, or use a stretch-and-fold method in the bowl.
Return the dough to the bowl, cover with a clean tea towel and leave at room temperature for 4–6 hours, or until doubled in size.
Shape the dough into a round loaf by tucking the edges underneath, then place in a lightly floured proving basket or bowl.
Cover again and leave to rise for 2–3 hours, or overnight in the fridge for better flavour.
Preheat the oven to 220°C and place a lidded casserole dish or Dutch oven inside to heat up.
When ready to bake, carefully remove the dish, place the dough inside, score the top with a sharp knife and cover with the lid.
Bake for 20 minutes with the lid on, then remove the lid and bake for another 20 minutes until golden brown and crusty.
Leave to cool on a wire rack before slicing. Best served fresh with a little plant-based butter or dipped in olive oil.
